questions.q: How do Swing and AWT differ?
options: Swing is lightweight and pure Java; AWT uses heavyweight native peers
AWT is lightweight; Swing is native
questions.explain: Swing components are drawn by Java itself (platform independent, pluggable look and feel). AWT wraps OS widgets.

questions.q: Contextual awareness in GUI design means the interface…
options: Adapts to the user's situation (location, role, device, task)
questions.explain: Ways to realise it: adapting content to the user's context, and context-sensitive help/menus.

questions.q: Which is part of the Java Foundation Classes besides Swing and AWT?
questions.explain: JFC also includes the Java 2D API, Accessibility API and drag-and-drop (data transfer).

questions.q: Which is NOT a component of the Z layout?
questions.explain: Z layout: eyes scan the top horizontal, then diagonal, then bottom horizontal.

questions.q: Controls vs containers in GUI design?
options: Controls are what the user interacts with; containers hold/store components
Containers are buttons; controls are panels
Controls hold components; containers are clickable
questions.explain: Controls: JButton, JTextField. Containers: JFrame, JPanel.

questions.q: Which is a type of consistency in GUI design?
questions.explain: Also functional, internal and external consistency.

questions.q: KPLC tariff (0–50 @10, 51–200 @15). Bill for 120 units?
questions.explain: 50×10=500 plus 70×15=1,050, total 1,550. Show the result in a JTextField.

questions.q: Which is NOT a part of Model-View-Controller?
questions.explain: Model=data/logic, View=display, Controller=handles input and updates both.

flashcards.a: AWT: heavyweight, uses native OS peers, platform look, fewer components. Swing: lightweight pure Java, pluggable look-and-feel, richer components (JButton, JTable), built on AWT.
GUI adapts to the user's context (location, role, device, task). Realised by: context-sensitive help/menus; adapting content or layout from user data, device or sensors.

flashcards.q: 1.3 Three other Java Foundation Classes parts (6)
flashcards.a: Java 2D API, Java Accessibility API, Java Beans API (from your notes; also drag-and-drop).
Visual (same fonts, colours, icons, layout) and functional (same action behaves the same everywhere). Also internal and external.
Top horizontal line (logo/navigation); diagonal line (eye moves to bottom-left); bottom horizontal line (call to action).
Controls: what the user interacts with (JButton, JTextField). Containers: hold and organise components (JFrame, JPanel).

flashcards.q: 2.i Swing components for bus billing + justify (6)
flashcards.a: JFrame (window), JComboBox (destination), JSpinner/JTextField (seats), JLabel (captions), JButton (Compute), non-editable JTextField (total).
Title bar; Destination combo (Thika/Juja/Ruiru); Passengers field; Compute Fare button; Total field at the bottom.
Input validation with clear messages; sensible defaults; tooltips/labels; consistent layout and colours; keyboard shortcuts; fast feedback; accessibility.
JFrame with JLabel + JTextField (units), JButton 'Compute Bill', non-editable JTextField (result); GridLayout or BorderLayout.

In the button's ActionListener: int u=Integer.parseInt(unitsField.getText()); double b; if(u<=50) b=u*10; else if(u<=200) b=500+(u-50)*15; else if(u<=500) b=2750+(u-200)*20; else b=8750+(u-500)*25; billField.setText(String.valueOf(b));  (500+2250=2750; +6000=8750)
Easier maintenance and debugging; reuse of modules; parallel team development and testing; better readability.
Model (data and logic); View (display); Controller (takes input, updates model and view).
Higher memory/CPU use; costlier and slower to develop; slower for expert users than command line; hard to automate/script; needs display hardware; can be cluttered.

flashcards.q: 5.i Java code to UPDATE a record (8)
flashcards.a: String sql="UPDATE student_details SET first_name=?, last_name=?, course=? WHERE reg_no=?"; PreparedStatement ps=con.prepareStatement(sql); ps.setString(1,fn); ps.setString(2,ln); ps.setString(3,course); ps.setString(4,reg); ps.executeUpdate();  (inside Update button's actionPerformed, in try/catch)

flashcards.q: 5.ii Java code to DELETE a record (6)
flashcards.a: PreparedStatement ps=con.prepareStatement("DELETE FROM student_details WHERE reg_no=?"); ps.setString(1,reg); ps.executeUpdate();

flashcards.q: 5.iii Three alternative events to search by reg number (6)
flashcards.a: Press Enter in the reg-number field (ActionListener); focusLost on that field; keyReleased (type-ahead search); selecting a row/item from a JTable or JComboBox; form load.
